text.p: Cephalon Inc and Chiron Corp said Tuesday they have submitted a new drug application to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration seeking clearance to market Myotrophin in injectable form in the United States for the treatment of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis.
The companies said the application contains findings from two double-blind, placebo-controlled, Phase 3 clinical studies of 449 patients with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis.
The Phase 3 studies were designed to measure patients' signs and symptoms of the ailment, overall well-being and health-related quality of life, they added.

They said that the FDA designated Myotrophin injection an orphan drug for the treatment of the ailment in 1991. That status is given to drugs that have been developed for serious diseases affecting a relatively small population. The drug is exclusive to its developers for a specified period.

The medicine is currently being made available to a limited number of patients with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis in the U.S. under a Treatment Investigational New Drug protocol approved by the FDA in June 1996, they said.

Cephalon and Chiron are developing Myotrophin injection in North America and Europe for the treatment of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis and other neuromuscular disorders, and are currently preparing applications for marketing approval in Canada and Europe.
Chiron, based in Emeryville, Calif., is a health care company that combines diagnostic, vaccine, and therapeutic strategies for controlling disease.
Cephalon, with headquarters in West Chester, Penn., is an international biopharmaceutical company that develops and markets products to treat neurological disorders.
